statement: Let n>=2 and c_j(n)=n*(n^2-1+3*2^(j-1)-3^j)/3. If c_j(n) is nonzero for every 1<=j<=n, then every n-element multiset of positive real numbers, including repetitions, is uniquely determined by the cardinality and first n logarithmic power sums of its complete Schur-(2,2) monomial-value multiset, with tableau multiplicities. This condition holds for every n>=3 with n!=4 and n modulo 60 outside {14,26,34,46}. Moreover, lengths 2 and 4 are uniquely reconstructible when the positive input sum is prescribed. Consequently, for every integer N>=2, positive integer partitions lambda,mu of N of length at least two and common length outside {14,26,34,46} modulo 60 satisfy S22(lambda)=S22(mu) only if lambda=mu. Equal output cardinalities force equal lengths. No converse, counterexample at an excluded length, or all-length resolution is claimed. Exact scope and proofs are Theorems A--C of evidence/research-moment-proof.md.
contribution: Proposed reconstruction application of established triangular power-sum methods and the known Chern-shadow coefficient formalism to shape (2,2). It gives an explicit sufficient length criterion and a positive-real injectivity theorem, with a fixed-sum partition consequence covering all but four residue classes modulo 60. Prefix recovery and elementary boundary reductions are not claimed as new. No equivalent reconstruction theorem was located in the bounded primary-source comparison dated 2026-09-12; novelty and mathematical value remain for fresh referee assessment. The frozen original problem remains unresolved.
